name: Spooky Candle Designing - Art Workshop
description:
Join us for a fun, spooky-themed candle-making workshop at Atta Galatta on 30th October!

Choose your candle/design theme.
Design, decorate, and personalise your candles.
Use the provided colours, decorative elements, and Halloween-inspired materials.
Get creative with spooky, quirky and fun designs.

All workshop materials will be provided.

name: Food In Literature - Book Club
description:
A journey is never just about the distance travelled; it is also about the lives, struggles, and hopes carried along the way. In “The Long March”, Namita Waikar turns our attention to India’s farmers and the realities that shape their lives, tracing stories of resilience, protest, and the fight to be heard. What can their journey teach us about rural India, inequality, and the people whose labour sustains the country yet so often remains unseen?
Book of the month: The Long March by Namita Waikar
When: Saturday, 31st October, 2026 at 11 a.m.
Where: Atta Galatta Bookstore, Indira Nagar
Ages: 18+
Hosted by: Prachi Grover
Registration is mandatory as we have limited spots.
The session is free & copies of the book are available at the store. 
Prachi Grover is a culinary consultant and educator and is the founder of “From Words to Wok,” a community for people who love to read and eat.

name: Public Disappearances - Book launch
description:
Join us on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 11 AM for an intimate literary morning celebrating the launch of Public Disappearances: Saunters and Sojourns in Europe by the acclaimed poet Debasish Lahiri.
Conceived in the utter solitude of worldly ruminations, this evocative poetry collection offers a profound exploration of place, memory, and the common incongruities of human experience. Written during extended periods of living across several European nations, the poems capture a distinct perspective that shifts seamlessly between the intimate gaze of the insider and the detached observation of the outsider.
Whether wandering through bustling historic streets or pausing in quiet, forgotten corners, the evening will immerse you in the quiet saunters and reflective sojourns that shaped this deeply moving work.
The discussions will also look at the role of European art in the shaping of the poetry, bringing into purview his ekphrastic book A Certain Penance of Light as well.

name: The Parenting Journey - Panel Discussion
description: This is an open and insightful conversation for parents navigating neurodivergence. Through personal experiences and expert perspectives, we will explore what neurodivergence means, the realities of the parenting journey, and ways to support children beyond academics. A space to learn, connect, and leave feeling more informed, supported, and hopeful about the journey ahead.

name: AG Lit Sisters Presents: Her Many Avatars: Goddesses in Indian Mythology - Thematic Book Club
description:
With Diwali around the corner, AG Lit Sisters invites readers to explore the fascinating world of goddesses in Indian mythology and literature.
From Lakshmi and Saraswati to Durga and Kali, and from Sita and Draupadi to contemporary mythological retellings, we'll explore the many stories, interpretations and representations of the feminine divine. Through books, folklore and literary retellings, we'll discuss themes of power, wisdom, courage, devotion, sacrifice, agency and rebellion, while revisiting familiar stories through fresh perspectives.
Members are welcome to bring a book about an Indian goddess, a mythological retelling, a collection of folklore, or simply their curiosity about these timeless stories.
As always, readers are welcome, but non-readers are celebrated! The session is open to anyone who enjoys stories and thoughtful conversations, whether or not they've read a book for the theme.

name: A Reading Circle with Dr. Ishita Dey - food in literature book club
description:
What can sweets tell us about caste, labour, migration, heritage and identity?
In Sweet Excess: Crafting Mishti in Bengal, Dr. Ishita Dey follows the making, selling and eating of mishti across West Bengal and Bangladesh. Drawing on a decade of ethnographic research, she takes us into sweet shops, workshops, homes, fairs and festivals to look closely at the people and systems behind a food that is so deeply woven into everyday life. The book asks us to look beyond sweetness and celebration: who makes our sweets, how is this work shaped by caste and religion, what happens when ideas of food safety and regulation enter traditional craft, and how does a food associated with abundance exist within a region marked by histories of hunger and food insecurity?
For this session we’ll gather as a reading circle, bringing our questions, observations and responses to the book into a shared conversation with Ishita.
About the Author:
Dr Ishita Dey is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Sociology, South Asian University, Delhi, and the author of Sweet Excess: Crafting Mishti in Bengal (Routledge, 2026). Her research explores food, labour, smell, infrastructure and migration, with a particular interest in the social worlds and histories around food. Her work has appeared in several journals including Contributions to Indian Sociology, Gastronomica, Senses and Society, and South Atlantic Quarterly. She has also been involved in several collaborative research projects exploring food and the senses, including work on the smells of Delhi. She is a member of the editorial collective of Gastronomica and the co-editor of Society and Culture in South Asia.
About the Moderator:
Prachi Grover is a culinary consultant and educator and is the founder of “From Words to Wok”; a community for people who to love to read and eat! Her work sits at the intersection of food, literature and culture.
Registration is mandatory as we have limited spots (link in bio)
The session is free & copies of the book are available at the store

name: Breaking the News - Media Literacy Workshop
description:
News finds us everywhere: on Instagram, WhatsApp, television, articles, newspapers, and even opinion reels.
Today, children are growing up in a digital world where information comes at them from every direction, with misinformation, disinformation, and AI-altered content increasingly woven into what they consume. Because of this, it becomes an essential skill to make sense of it, recognize different perspectives, and decide what deserves our trust.
Breaking the News helps children look beyond the headlines and understand how the news they consume is created and shaped.
Our Method:
Children step into the shoes of reporters and investigate a news event through fun roleplay and interactive challenges. They uncover different perspectives and explore their choices about what to include, leave out, and how that can shape the public narrative.
What They Will Leave With:
Children will:

Learn to recognise misinformation, propaganda, disinformation and AI-altered content.
Build the habit of questioning, comparing sources, and looking for evidence before forming an opinion.
Understand how media representation shapes what we see as important or unimportant.
Build curiosity about current affairs and the world around them.

Who Should Attend:
This workshop is ideal for parents who want their child to:

Learn to read and engage with news critically, not passively.
Build news and media literacy in an increasingly digital world.
Understand how different perspectives can shape the way we see an issue.
Develop the habit of questioning information, seeking evidence, and thinking for themselves.
Become more thoughtful and informed participants in the world around them.

name: The Banana Tusker - Theatre Performance
description:
One fine day, Teja’s friends discovered that he was missing from his home. They decided to go on a journey to find him.

name: Kurukshetra - A storytelling deep-dive
description:
Every culture has a night when the dead come closer. Long before modern campfire tales, the Mahabharata recorded nights when shadows held daggers, man-eating monsters went on rampages, and the dead climbed out of dark river waters to speak with the living.
Join Aparna Jaishankar as she shares ominous, spine chilling tales from the many Mahabharatas found across cultures

name: Live Drawing Bootcamp - Art Workshop
description:

Age Group: 15+

name: KALIGHAT PAINTINGS - WHERE TRADITION MEETS MODERNITY
description:
Step into the vibrant world of Kalighat Painting, one of Bengal's most distinctive folk-art traditions, in an immersive workshop.
This workshop goes beyond simply creating a painting. It is an opportunity to discover the story, culture, history, and visual language behind Kalighat art and understand how this traditional art form evolved with changing times.
Beginning with the origins of Kalighat paintings in 19th-century Kolkata, the workshop explores the artistic community of Patuas, the influence of the Kalighat Temple, and the bustling world around it that shaped this unique art tradition.
Participants will discover how Kalighat artists moved from depicting Hindu deities and mythological stories to portraying everyday life, contemporary society, humour, and social observations. Through these works, the paintings became a fascinating visual record of Bengal's changing social landscape.
A key part of the workshop will be understanding the distinctive Kalighat visual language—its confident flowing lines, bold contours, expressive figures, simplified forms, and vibrant compositions. We will also explore how Bengal's folk traditions influenced modern Indian art, particularly through the work of Jamini Roy.
The session combines storytelling, art appreciation, visual references, demonstrations, and hands-on practice, allowing participants to first understand the tradition and then interpret it through their own artwork.
Participants will be guided through the process of creating a Kalighat-inspired painting, making the experience both educational and creative. No prior art experience is required—just curiosity and a willingness to explore.
WHAT YOU WILL EXPERIENCE

The fascinating history and evolution of Kalighat Painting
Stories behind its mythological, social, and everyday-life themes
An exploration of the Patuas and the Kalighat tradition
The influence of Jamini Roy and Bengal's folk-art vocabulary
Understanding of lines, forms, colours, composition, and expression
A guided hands-on Kalighat-inspired painting session
Your own completed artwork to take home

Through Hues by Sindhoor, this workshop aims to make traditional Indian art experiential rather than simply instructional—giving participants the opportunity to connect with a living artistic tradition through its stories, forms, and their own creative expression.
Come discover Kalighat—not just as a style of painting, but as a window into Bengal's history, culture, people, and imagination.

name: Kalimpong - Book Launch
description:
This is the book launch event for a novel by Debalina Haldar, a Sahitya Akademi-shortlisted novelist. This is her fourth novel, “Kalimpong”.
About the book
1949, Tibet. Five-year-old Pema and her inseparable friend Dama spend their days chasing dreams through mountain villages, studying at the local school, and praying at the monastery. But when conflict sweeps through Tibet, their peaceful childhood is shattered. As the political turmoil peaks, a single act of betrayal changes the course of their lives forever.
Years later, in the mist-laden mountain town of Kalimpong, a woman begins searching for the story behind a bracelet engraved with names she does not recognize. Drawn by an inexplicable connection, she uncovers a forgotten story that stretches from the snowbound valleys of Tibet to the refugee settlements of India—a story of enduring friendship, sibling love, impossible choices, exile and belonging, and of mothers and daughters whose lives were shaped by history's upheavals.
Rich with the landscapes of the Eastern Himalayas and infused with the enduring presence of clouds, rivers, and memory, Kalimpong: The Ridge of Lost Names is a novel about the names history forgets and the love that remembers them.
About the Author
Debalina Haldar is an alumna of IIM Lucknow, class of 2015. She started writing when she was seven years old. She writes in the literary fiction genre. Her novel, The Female Ward, was published in October 2012, by Thames River Press (UK). Her second book, Wrinkles in Memory, is a collection of 22 short stories. It was published in August 2016 by Lifi Publications. Wrinkles in Memory was shortlisted for the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar for books in English in 2020. Her novel, The Daughters of Shantiniketan, was published in August 2025 by Readomania Publishing. She is based in Bengaluru, where she lives with her husband and her two children.

name: Coffee and Conversations - Meetup
description:
What about some Filter Coffee and Unfiltered conversations on a fine Sunday morning?
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment.
We at Listeners Circle are committed to building a community where there are no unsaid words, held-back emotions and buried feelings because of the fear of being judged.
After 50+ Editions of Tell Your Story, Listeners Circle is relaunching a lighter format - Coffee and Conversations!
Coffee lightens us up. Coffee gives us clarity. Coffee refreshes. Sip a coffee and speak your heart out without fear of judgment, and listen without judging! Coffee is on us, and the onus of conversation without judgment is on you.
 
Every word matters. Every emotion matters. Every feeling matters.
Think about how it would feel to take an hour out of your fast-paced life and share your experiences and thoughts to people who listen to you without judging over a cup of Coffee? Also, listen to others without judging.
Listeners' Circle Coffee and Conversations -This is an event to make that happen.
 
Be a part of the Listener's Circle Coffee & Conversations - Edition 5.
Speak your mind without being judged. Speak your mind without any boundaries. No photography and videography without consent. Your stories stay within the four walls of the room and the hearts.
Would you like to just listen? We have a place for you too.
Book your passes in advance to avoid the last-minute sell outs.
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment. We have done 50+ sessions over the last year, enabling people to voice their stories. Coffee & Conversations is our new format based on popular demand.

name: Authentic Relating Games  - Playful yet deep games to help people connect
description:
Ever wonder what is possible when we drop the small talk and connect for real?

Authentic Relating Games is a global practice of guided, playful yet deep exercises (the 'games') designed to help people connect more honestly and meaningfully — whether with close friends or complete strangers.

Through structured partner and group conversations, you will get to practice speaking from the heart, deep listening, and noticing what's alive in you as you relate to others.  The games create space for more honesty, curiosity, and real human connection — often in ways that feel surprisingly fun, refreshing, and profoundly moving.

What to Expect

- A Structured Container:  We will start as a full group to set some simple guidelines that ensure the space feels safe, respectful, and confidential.
- Activities with Partners, Trios, and the Large Group: We'll keep changing partners throughout the session (no need to bring a partner!).
- Guided Prompts and Demos: We'll guide you step-by-step through the games and provide live demonstrations so you know what to do.
- Total Autonomy: You are always in the driver's seat.  You choose how deeply you want to go, or pass on a prompt or game at any time.
- A New Set of Games: If you attended Authentic Relating Games previously, don't worry this won't be the same games but a different set of activities to explore!

No experience needed.  Come as you are.  If you've never done anything like this before, don't worry — it's simple and there is no pressure to get it "right".

About the facilitator:
Roy Jacob is the founder of the Conscious Communication Academy and has been facilitating workshops and retreats for over 15 years, mostly for changemakers as well as team retreats for NGOs and companies.  Roy grew up in the U.S. before finding his calling and coming to India (where his roots are) in 2003.  He believes in the transformative power of combining radical honesty with radical care.

name: Mycelium & Muse - A Science Storytelling Workshop
description:
We often equate creativity with making art. Picasso was creative. Beethoven was creative. Van Gogh was creative. But what about the person who first picked up a piece of charcoal and scribbled on the wall of a cave, hoping the people in the next cave would get  the message? Or the bowerbird who spends an entire season collecting blue bottle caps and flowers to decorate a little stage for a Mate? And what about a fungus? This one is literally brainless, yet it sends out electrical signals that, when connected to a synthesiser, play out like music. So if creativity shows up in organisms without brains, it is far older than us, isn't it?
That's the question we'll sit with: 
Where does creativity really begin on the tree of life, and what does that mean for all of us who have spent years saying "I'm just not the creative type". Along the way, you'll hear a mushroom playing music, make an idea card that is deliberately, wonderfully bad, write a letter to your future self, and discover a new answer to the question “Am I creative?” You don't need any science background to join in. Just come in, and let's get some creativity
Brewing. Because, tell you what, we are not sure if a creative life is a happier one. But we can absolutely guarantee that it's a far more meaningful one.
 
About the facilitator: 
Bitasta Datta is a microbiologist by training, an educator by profession and a science storyteller by passion.
For over 10 years, she has been turning science into stories for school learners and curious adults. She started at the National Digital Library of India, went on to co-found The Synapse, led curriculum and learning experience design at BYJU'S and Tutopiya, and now leads the efforts at Khan Academy India to narrate science in a way that sticks.
She believes science and art are two lenses on the same world, and that if you look through both long enough, you arrive at the same philosophy. So that's what she does. She dissects science to find the art in it, dissects art to find the science in it, and narrates her findings as stories.
Outside work, she paints, bakes, and travels, and writes about the places where science, art and philosophy run into each other. Mycelium & Muse began as one of those pieces

name: Demystifying the P word - Poetry Workshop
description:
Do you find poetry inaccessible, opaque, difficult to read and appreciate?
As the oldest form of literature, right from the oral tradition, poetry has always been the way humans told their stories. From Gilgamesh to Homer, from Kalidasa to Wordsworth, from Neruda to Akhmatova, poetry has brought us tales of love and loss and beauty and war.
If you want to explore poetry, learn ways to break it down, understand its nuances, its special code, its peculiar love language, then join us as we run you through a selection of poems that let you develop a set of hacks that you can employ when you read your next poem.
Whether you are just curious, a poetry enthusiast still trying to figure it out, or a poet hoping to expand your writing horizon, there is something here for you to listen to, learn from, and laugh with. Come, hear the stories behind the poems and the poems behind the stories.  
About Alt Poetry:
Alt Poetry is a multi-channel poetry platform that brings poets, readers, and poetry lovers together to read, discover, and debate poetry from all around the world. We host different events online and in-person, including ‘Poet of the Month’, ‘Book Talk’, ‘Poetry Atlas ’, and ‘Poetry Classroom’.
Alt Poetry is founded by Namratha Varadharajan (Author: On Cultivating Loudspeakers and Quilts -forthcoming from Booksthakam), Madhuri Katti (Author: Life, Time, and Other Things), and Rajani Radhakrishnan (Author: Water to Water, Duplicity, and No Way Home)
Limited spots available.

name: Lino Print Workshop - Art Workshop
description:
This hands-on workshop introduces the basics of lino cut printmaking, from carving a simple design to inking and printing your own artwork. Participants will be guided through the process step by step and will leave with their own prints, perfect as small artworks or gifts.
The session runs for three hours and includes demonstrations, supported making time, and space to experiment.
Open to beginners and anyone curious about printmaking — no prior experience needed. Suitable for ages 14+.
What should I bring?
Clothes you don’t mind getting messy in, ideas or finished sketches for designs (found images from books are welcome), and lots of creativity.
What’s provided?
All printing tools, paper, and inks will be provided.
What do I take home?
All finished artworks are yours to keep, along with any unfinished pieces. Participants will also keep their carved lino block, allowing them to reprint at home with basic supplies.
What's included:

Lino sheet
Lino carving tool
Lino ink
140gsm paper
Baren
Roller

name: Submergence - Book Signing
description:
Join us at Atta Galatta for a special book signing with Anjali M S, a young, up-and-coming author who is about to release her YA dystopian book Submergence. Submergence is a dystopian novel set in a future where wars, pollution, and a catastrophic asteroid impact have submerged nearly all of Earth, leaving behind one continent divided between two rival governments. While one fights to restore the dying planet, the other looks to space travel for humanity’s salvation. Caught between these opposing ideologies are a spy and a murderous soldier whose fates are dangerously intertwined.
Come meet Anjali, discover her work, and get your copy signed. Whether you're an enthusiastic reader, an aspiring writer, or simply someone who loves a good story, this is an opportunity to connect with a young author and celebrate the joy of books.


Date: 23 January 2027


Time: 2:00–3:00 PM


Venue: Atta Galatta, Bengaluru


Instagram handle: @anjalims_author


Format: Author meet-and-greet and book signing


Age Group: 12+ 


We look forward to welcoming readers for an afternoon celebrating books, storytelling, and the next generation of authors.
